name: Lucia Webb
life: “I still remember different languages using the same word for thunder.” People around Studio Boulevard know Lucia by a small Sunday habit. Lucia waits by the window where the whole crossing can be seen without leaning into the road.
voice: I came to interpret for one family and ended up translating an argument about a wet dog.
appearance: Lucia is easy to recognize by short copper curls and a round face with a pronounced chin. Usually dressed in a boxy denim jacket with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light, Lucia touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word when listening.
personality: Lucia can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To let each family hear the wet-dog story correctly.
family: Esme Valejo is Lucia’s stepsibling. Lucia brings something that can still be enjoyed tomorrow. Esme checks the date twice. Arrangements do change in their family. Taking a delay seriously without treating it as an insult took both of them years. Asked about *The empty berth*, Esme says, “I put a price on a storm that might come once in fifty years.”
connections: Nora Nolasco. The petitions reach signers in more than one language.

reactions.situation: Rain blurs the names on the petition
reactions.response: Lucia records the petitioners who are present and asks them how to recover the others.

reactions.situation: Somebody finds a lost wallet outside the bank
reactions.response: Lucia asks the counter staff for a receipt so its return can be traced even after their shift changes.

reactions.situation: If a neighbor offers a costly present
reactions.response: Lucia asks for an afternoon to work out whether accepting it would put someone else in debt.
